title: add jsonschema response_format strict mode + improved validation/errors (openai-compat)
author: Ava Martinez
description: Context: customers and internal evals require deterministic structured outputs for downstream parsing and tool-calling. This PR introduces a server-side JSONSchema-based response_format with an opt-in strict mode that enforces schema conformance and surfaces clearer error messages when the model output does not match the schema. Motivation: reduce engineering debt in downstream parsers, provide OpenAI-compat behavior for 'response_format' while keeping low-latency streaming for non-strict workflows. Summary of changes: 1) API layer: add response_format.type == "json_schema" and response_format.strict (boolean, default false) to request protobuf/REST contract; 2) Validation pipeline: introduce server-side validator that attempts streaming-friendly incremental validation but falls back to buffered validation when strict==true to guarantee full JSON conformance; 3) Error model: new structured error codes (INVALID_SCHEMA_OUTPUT, PARTIAL_JSON_STREAM, VALIDATION_FAILED) with helpful messages and optional 'repair_suggestions' hint returned in error metadata; 4) OpenAI compat: add compatibility shims so requests using openai-style response_format map to the same validation semantics; 5) Docs and SDK: update TS/Python SDKs and docs examples to show strict vs non-strict behavior and migration notes; 6) Tests: add unit + integration tests that simulate streaming partials, malformed outputs, and model retries. Implementation notes: strict mode buffers model tokens server-side until a complete JSON value is produced and validated; to avoid large memory usage we enforce a configurable buffer limit (default 64KB) and return VALIDATION_FAILED with code PARTIAL_JSON_STREAM if exceeded. For streaming with strict==false we continue to stream tokens and attach a trailing validation result when the response ends (non-blocking). To preserve latency for low-latency workloads strict is opt-in. Rollout plan: feature gated behind a runtime flag and beta release; default remains strict=false. Migration: SDKs expose response_format.strict flag; customers doing strict parsing should migrate to strict=true to get server-side guarantees. Observability: new metrics (response_format.validation.failures, response_format.validation.latency, response_format.buffer_overflow) and traces added to console dashboards. Backwards compatibility: openai compat layer maps old response_format shapes into new schema; no behavior change unless strict=true. Checklist: - [x] API contract + server validation pipeline - [x] OpenAI compatibility shims - [x] tests (unit + integration) - [x] docs + SDK examples - [x] metrics + alerts - [x] feature flag + rollout notes

feat(runtime): add incremental validator and strict-mode buffering with buffer limit

test: add unit and integration tests for streaming+strict validation

release_notes: Add a JSONSchema-based response_format with an opt-in strict mode for guaranteed server-side validation; introduces stable error codes for structured output validation and OpenAI compatibility mapping. Default remains non-strict. See docs for migration and rollout details.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated behind runtime flag response_format.jsonschema.enabled=false by default; in strict mode watch response_format.buffer_overflow and validation.failure rates. Buffer limit default 64KB and configurable via runtime config.
